CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who sustained a left ankle injury yesterday while walking with his wife. He stepped off a curb and landed incorrectly on the ankle. He denies hearing a pop but describes the ankle feeling extended and stretched. Pain is localized to the outside of the ankle. He was able to walk home after the incident but with significant difficulty and pain. Symptoms have persisted for approximately one to two days. Denies any significant prior injuries to this ankle. Patient has been self-treating with ibuprofen, elevation, ice, and weight-bearing avoidance. Current pain level is 8/10 without medication, decreasing to approximately 7/10 with ibuprofen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No other systems reviewed in this focused visit.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history documented.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen (patient-initiated)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is married and works from home. He and his wife frequently take walks together for exercise and recreation.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: Stable but slightly elevated, attributed to pain
Focused ankle exam: Ecchymosis and bruising noted over the lateral malleolus with associated swelling and edema. Tenderness to palpation on the lateral side with soft tissue swelling. No joint laxity appreciated. No bony tenderness to palpation of the foot.
Neurovascular exam of left foot: Capillary refill brisk at less than three seconds. Dorsalis pedis pulses strong bilaterally. Motor and sensory function intact and symmetric bilaterally.

RESULTS
X-ray of left ankle: No fracture or bony abnormalities identified.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left ankle pain consistent with lateral ligament complex ankle sprain. Continue RICE protocol with elevation, compression, and ice. Prescribed air cast for ankle stabilization. Prescribed crutches with instructions to remain off the leg but begin walking as tolerated as symptoms improve. Continue NSAIDs for pain and swelling management. Expect significant symptom improvement over 4-7 days. Follow-up appointment scheduled in two weeks. Patient instructed to return to clinic if symptoms worsen significantly or for any other concerns.
